messages.author: b65e4adb82fabb92
messages.subject: greek y-label
parts:
Hi Ggplot2 Users,

I'm pretty new to ggplot2. I've a simple question.

I want to change y=label including greek letters. How can I do it? I'm
not even familiar with where to put y-label statement. I need
something like this:

ylab=expression(mu*g/m^3)

# R Code
p <- ggplot(mtcars, aes(factor(cyl), mpg))
p + geom_boxplot() + coord_flip()

Thanks in advance, Happy holidays,
Xin

messages.author: 5a1b5a9591c118ef
messages.subject: Re: greek y-label
parts:
Hi,

try this,

last_plot() + ylab(expression(mu*g/m^3))

(note that the label is at the bottom because of coord_flip).

HTH,

baptiste

messages.author: 5a1b5a9591c118ef
messages.subject: Re: greek y-label
parts:
Hi,

Your example didn't have a legend so it's hard to give a specific
answer. The general idea is to use scale_xx_yy() to set the legend
title. For instance, if your legend is mapped to the colour,

p <- ggplot(mtcars, aes(factor(cyl), mpg,colour=cyl))
p + geom_boxplot() + coord_flip() + scale_colour_continuous("Change me")

HTH,

baptiste

I'm sorry about that, I got this self-running code from r-help. In this case, how can I change my legend title (currently its "factor(g)".
 
Also, can you please suggest me some good reference to learn more about ggplot2. It seems to be a little different from standard R syntax. Thanks a lot!

# R Code
g <- rep.int(c("A", "B", "C", "D"), 125)
t <- rnorm(5000)
a <- sample(t, 500, replace=TRUE)
b <- sample(t, 500, replace=TRUE)
dta <- data.frame(val = sample(t,1000), g = gl(4, 250, labels=c("A", "B",
"C", "D")) , G2 = gl(2,1, labels=c("XX", "YY")))
# ggplot2 package required
p <- ggplot(dta, aes(factor(G2), val))
p + geom_boxplot(aes(fill = factor(g)))
